summary: This note describes the Socialist Party of Oregon's presence in Columbia County, Oregon, which began around the First Red Scare. It says that in 1914 the party had 27 more registered members than the Prohibition Party and was similar to the Progressive Party in trying to effect change from outside government. The note also says the party received press attention despite failing its first year, noting the October Revolution in Russia led by Vladimir Lenin.
one_line: Overview of the Socialist Party of Oregon in Columbia County, its early membership in 1914, and its place among local reform parties.
key_facts: The Socialist Party of Oregon in Columbia County, Oregon began around the First Red Scare.
In its first year (1914) of going mainstream, the Socialist Party had 27 more registered members than the Prohibition Party.
The Prohibition Party's members were described as some members of the Suffrage movement.
The Socialist Party was similar to the Progressive Party in Columbia County, as both tried to make change from the outskirts of government.
The Socialist Party failed in its first year but still received attention from the press.
The press was aware of the October Revolution (1918) in Russia, which is now the Soviet Union.
The October Revolution was led by a similarly named government under Vladimir Lenin.
